sections.h2: Where do I record a deed in Surry County?
sections.html:
Deeds for land in Surry County are recorded at the Register of Deeds office at 201 East Kapp Street in Dobson, mailing address P.O. Box 303, Dobson, NC 27017. The main number is (336) 401-8150, and the real estate fax line is (336) 401-8149.

The county lists office hours of 8:15 am to 5:00 pm Monday through Friday, with Tuesday opening at 9:00 am. Real estate documents are accepted for recording from 8:15 am to 4:30 pm Monday through Friday, so a closing package that arrives at 4:45 pm will wait for the next business day. Check the county page before a Tuesday morning drop-off.

Surry County has about 72,287 residents spread over 532.65 square miles of land. A seller anywhere in the county records at this one office.

sections.h2: Does Surry County accept electronic recording?
sections.html:
Yes. The register's real estate page names two e-recording companies the office accepts documents from: Simplifile and Corporation Service Company.

Most title companies and closing attorneys already hold an account with one of them, which means a closing can be recorded without anyone driving to Dobson. If you are selling without an attorney, ask the person handling your closing how the deed will be submitted. The county page lists a phone number for Simplifile at (800) 460-5657 and a web address for Corporation Service Company.

  • Electronic submission goes through an approved vendor, not directly through the county website.
  • Paper deeds can be delivered in person or mailed to the P.O. Box.
  • The real estate fax line is separate from the vital records fax line, so use (336) 401-8149 only for real estate matters.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a deed in North Carolina?
sections.html:
Recording fees are set by statute and are the same in every county, including Surry. For an ordinary instrument, G.S. 161-10 sets $26.00 for the first 15 pages and $4.00 for each page after that, and the statute describes its fee list as complete and exclusive.

The register collects fees before filing a document. Deeds of trust and mortgages use a separate, higher schedule, which matters if your buyer is financing and your closer records both documents on the same day.

Statewide recording and excise tax terms as printed in the General Statutes
ItemAmount or ruleStatute
General instrument$26.00 for the first 15 pages, $4.00 per added pageG.S. 161-10
Deed of trust or mortgage$64.00 for the first 35 pages, $4.00 per added pageG.S. 161-10
Satisfaction or cancellation of a deed of trustNo feeG.S. 161-10
Excise tax on a deed$1.00 per $500.00 or fraction of the consideration or valueG.S. 105-228.30

sections.h2: Who pays the excise tax when a Surry County house sells?
sections.html:
The seller pays. State law says the transferor pays the tax to the register of deeds before the deed is recorded, at the rate of one dollar for each $500 of consideration or value, counting any fraction.

For a Surry County sale, that means the tax is normally taken from your side of the settlement statement and delivered to the Dobson office with the deed. Ask your closer to show you the line item before closing day. The county keeps half of what it collects for its general fund, and the rest goes to the Department of Revenue each month, with the county allowed to retain 2% of the State share.

If a parcel crosses into two counties, the tax is paid in the county that holds the greater value. Confirm the parcel layout with your closer if your acreage is large.

sections.h2: Why does recording order matter for a seller?
sections.html:
A deed is protected against later claims only from the moment it is registered in the county where the land lies. Under G.S. 47-18, conveyances, long leases, options and rights of first refusal are not valid against lien creditors or purchasers for value until they are registered, and priority follows the order of registration.

For a seller, this is the reason a closing is not finished when the buyer signs. Until the deed reaches the register, a creditor or another buyer could record first. Surry County takes recordings only during the 8:15 am to 4:30 pm window, and e-recording lets the closer submit the package without that delay.

After closing, ask your title company for the recording information, which shows the book and page or instrument number. That reference is how you or a future buyer will find the deed in the online record search.

sections.h2: How far back do the Surry County land records go?
sections.html:
The records start in 1771, the year Surry County was formed from Rowan County. At that time the county covered land that later became Stokes, Forsyth and Yadkin counties.

The register's page describes the early collection as including deeds from agents of Lord Granville, state land grants, sheriff's deeds, mortgages and property divisions. Original books can be viewed or copied through the imaging system, and they also exist on microfilm and in book form. The oldest index covers 1771 to 1870, and a second index runs from 1870 to 1937.

  • The early records include land grants from the state and deeds from agents of Lord Granville.
  • Land that now sits in Stokes, Forsyth or Yadkin may appear in early Surry volumes.
  • Online search and recording standards are linked from the real estate page.

If a title problem surfaces during a sale, a title examiner usually does this research. A seller can still look up the chain of ownership to find a missing release or an old easement.

sections.h2: Can personal information be removed from Surry County records online?
sections.html:
Yes, within limits. The county explains that G.S. 132-1.10(f) allows certain personal identifiers to be redacted from the website copy of a record, and it publishes a redaction request form.

The request must be in writing, signed by the requester or an agent with power of attorney, and must name the information and the document. Items that can be covered include Social Security numbers, driver's license and passport numbers, bank account numbers and card numbers or PINs. Only the website image changes. The official record kept in the deed vault stays as it was recorded.

This is worth knowing if you recorded an old deed that contains a number you would rather not have online. Call (336) 401-8150 before sending a request.

sections.h2: How does Surry County compare with nearby counties for sellers?
sections.html:
Surry County is a mid-sized rural county with a median value of owner-occupied homes of $177,600 for 2020 to 2024, according to Census QuickFacts. About 73.4% of housing units are owner-occupied, and the median household income for the same period is $55,656.

Union County shows a median home value of $417,300 in the same Census table, and Swain County in the mountains shows $207,000. The gap affects what a seller pays in excise tax, since the tax follows the price. It also means a Surry County deed is often a smaller transaction than one recorded in Monroe.

The county had 244 building permits in 2025 and 34,405 housing units as of July 2025. Whatever the reason for a sale, the deed ends up recorded at the Dobson office.

sections.h2: What should I bring to a Surry County closing?
sections.html:
Bring photo identification, the signed deed prepared by your attorney or title company, and any payoff statements for existing loans. If a mortgage is being paid off, the lender records a satisfaction, and the statute lists no recording fee for that document.

  • Deed in recordable form, following the county's recording standards.
  • Funds or authorization for the excise tax collected before recording.
  • A completed and notarized document if you are signing through an agent under a power of attorney.
  • Contact details for the person who will submit the deed, whether by e-recording or at the counter.

If heirs inherited the house, record the supporting estate paperwork the closing attorney tells you to, and ask the clerk of superior court about any probate steps. For a small estate, the clerk of the county where the owner lived handles the affidavit process.

faqs.q: What is the address of the Surry County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: It is 201 East Kapp Street, Dobson, NC 27017, with a mailing address of P.O. Box 303 and a main phone of (336) 401-8150. Recording of real estate documents runs 8:15 am to 4:30 pm Monday through Friday.

faqs.q: Can my closing company e-record a deed in Surry County?
faqs.a: Yes, through Simplifile or Corporation Service Company, the two vendors the office lists. Ask your closer which one they use.

faqs.q: Who pays the deed excise tax on a Surry County sale?
faqs.a: The seller does. G.S. 105-228.30 puts the tax on the transferor at $1.00 for each $500 of value, paid to the register before the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: How much does the register charge to record an ordinary deed?
faqs.a: The statewide charge for a general instrument is $26.00 for up to 15 pages plus $4.00 for each further page, under G.S. 161-10. Ask the office whether your document needs any add-on charges.

faqs.q: Does recording a deed change the property tax bill?
faqs.a: Recording moves ownership on the record, but the tax bill follows the parcel. Taxes are due September 1 and can be paid without interest until January 5, so settle that line with your closer. Ask the Surry County tax office for the current bill.
